title: From disengagement to re-engagement: behavioral evidence for AI-driven adaptive tutoring interventions in intelligent tutoring systems.
summary: Analysis of 597,242 ASSISTments records from 799 students over three years identified different patterns of disengagement and recovery. Random-forest feature analysis linked response time and hint use to engagement states; emotional labels remain provisional and the observational analysis does not establish intervention effects.
ai_technology: Random-forest feature analysis and longitudinal state-transition analysis

evidence.tested: Three years of tutoring-system records were analyzed; reported behavioral patterns varied by inferred engagement state.
evidence.unknown: Engagement labels are provisional; observational feature associations do not establish that adaptive interventions caused re-engagement.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest feature analysis and longitudinal state-transition analysis

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
